title: Six-class secp256k1 rho at 126.1891: 687-instruction step (meter deferred carry) and retuned headroom

claims.statement: For a uniform full-production secp256k1 input Q=[x]P, the classical cold six-class negation-plus-GLV parallel Pollard-rho attack described in proof.md and upstream-proof.md halts on every run with total work at most 2^126.1891 target-group-operation equivalents under classical-group-work-v2 (C=1000). The H1 calibration (kappa=1.01, q29 census) is unchanged from the accepted packages. The two free ledger parameters are retuned: Markov headroom h=0.0034836 (was 0.003866) and floor p0=0.3934889 (was 0.39388), giving p0 - h - 2e-7 = 0.3900051 > 0.390005 > 0.39. Peak memory is below 2^72 bytes; preprocessing is capped at 2^59 units, charged and included; nonuniform advice is zero. The ordinary step is repriced from 688 to 687 instructions: the meter's charge becomes ADDS #687 on its low word with B.CS to a rare carry path (expected total below 2^68.6 milli-units, inside the 2^70 other row; the same deferred-carry pattern as the accepted length row), so the length/meter/loop row drops 9 -> 8, rows 87 -> 86, and the step is 108 + 493 + 86 = 687; doubling is 837 and traversal 711. The counted kernels and loops are 5d3bf6c4's, byte for byte. Exact ledger: phase 1 = 2^126.1806549, hard extras = 2^112.7859107 (checkpoint writes 2^112.7565081), expected random extras = 2^110.5799723, allowance = ceil(extras/0.0034836) = 2^118.7451776, total W_ledger = 2^126.1890984 < 2^126.1891; the exact Markov ratio is 0.00348294 < 0.0034836. certificate.py proves the bound in exact integer and rational arithmetic, including W^10000 < 1000^10000*2^1261891 and W^10000 > 1000^10000*2^1261890. The claim is self-contained in proof.md; no prior acceptance, review verdict, official score or cross-submission comparison is a premise. The construction is credited as provenance and declared as a dependency on submission 5d3bf6c4. This is an analytic heuristic bound, not a practical break or executed production attack.

experiments.purpose: Part A: production secp256k1 checks of the walk identities and truncated canonical-index rule; Part B: a scaled sequential toy pipeline on configured subgroups of y^2=x^3+7 with an unreduced subgroup-order check, a T_c census, node routing, and a long-trail trap test; kernels: limb-for-limb Python ports of the generated field kernels (asserting every no-overflow step) checked against big integers and affine secp256k1, the shipped counted loops and emitter wrappers executed by an AArch64 interpreter (including reductions whose final fold fires), instruction counts parsed from the shipped assembly, and the work-meter ledger recomputed from the prices and rows of proof.md. The toy run does not meter production instructions or implement 2^20 concurrent walks.
